The evidence presented is not conclusive because it does not say which regions have the selection. Looking at the paper Table 2 shows that the signal regions require N b-jets = 0 but VRtt¯WZ in Table 7 has b-jets and MET selection. We should be abel to cover both types of queries - looking at what was covered in signal regions vs what was covered in validation or control regions. The answer here is "yes" or VR but "no" for SR. THis distinction is lost in the current schema so that needs to be fixed (making MRs now). Huge failure here. Search, b-tagged, and MET are all in the first evidenence section above. How is this not identified as a paper that matches? Looking into the paper, it uses the standard b-tagging algorithms requiring 2 b-jets in the SRs and also uses a less-common track-jet b-tagging algorithm. Most if not all SRs require at least 2 b-jets.

I agree that there is no explicit evidence for b-tagged jets, but with "events with top quark pairs" and " with exactly one isolated charged lepton" there has to be b-jets. It is expected from what is listed but not explicited listed. In the strict interpretation of evidence in this sentence alone, the answer is "no", in the sense of if I should keep looking at this paper in more detail to answer this question, the answer is "yes".

It seems from here that there is a MET and b-jet selection, but the b-jet selction is for a veto. I'd be hesitant to call a paper on this evidence for b-jet requirements. More information is needed to see if there are regions that look for the signal in top-enriched selections.

Definitely a search using b-jets. The MET selection is unclear but thre is a MET significance cut which usually implies a MET cut (especially since the cut is > not <). More evidence is needed to see what the MET cut value is, but my guess is there is one applied (more likely that not applied). In the strict interpretation of evidence in this sentence alone, the answer is "no", in the sense of if I should keep looking at this paper in more detail to answer this question, the answer is "yes".
